name: component-wall
title: Component Wall
author: AlgorizeTech
description: A landing hero for a component library: a headline that blurs in word by word and keeps one word turning, a lead, an install command that names whichever card a camera has just landed on, two actions, a line of trust and the tools it is built with in batches — centred between two walls of screenshots that never end, one camera resting high and the other low, or on the left of a single wall.
docs:
Named export: ComponentWall (plus the ComponentWallItem type). Composed from the image-wall, text-animation, copy-button, avatar-stack and half-stars items, which install alongside it, and takes a tech-stack in its `stack` slot. Pass `badge` ({ label, href? }), `heading` (a string, revealed word by word; write `{word}` where `headingWords` take turns every `wordInterval` ms, and name one word in `accent` for the primary colour), `description` (a string or inline JSX — it renders inside a

), `install` ({ command } — write `{item}` where the focused card's `slug` goes, e.g. `npx shadcn@latest add @algorize-ui/{item}`), `primaryAction`/`secondaryAction` ({ label, href, icon? }), `trust` ({ text, avatars?, rating? }), `items` ({ title, image, slug? }[] — every screenshot sits in the same 493:332 frame; slug defaults to the title in kebab-case) and `stack` (a node — a of s of : the tools over the lower wall on desktop and under the band on phones; in the centred layout it closes the copy column, where the compact variant fits). `columns`, `interval` (ms the camera rests; 0 holds still), `order` (serial | shuffle), `zoom`, `intro` (ms the camera drifts with nothing in focus while the copy arrives; default 1800) and `onFocus` pass straight to the wall; `layout` is split (copy left, wall right) or center (copy between two walls — the left camera resting high, the right low, taking turns, the second wall dealing the same items from halfway through; the tools sit under the copy; zoom defaults to 0.9; below lg a single band of every card sits between the copy and the tools); `linkComponent` takes next/link. The headline uses your theme's font-serif, the command font-mono; colours are theme tokens.
